correctness.rationale: The Arens--Eells molecule norming argument reduces the operator norm to images of every normalized pair molecule. For rooted pairs the answer is the symbol modulus. McShane extension establishes that the three-point Lipschitz hexagon is the entire feasible two-coordinate projection; all its vertices are enumerated, including equality cases of the triangle inequality. Evaluating the three antipodal vertex pairs gives the exact formula. Checking selectors and sign choices yields the precise constants. Independent local exact rational tests passed 7000 and full finite global LP tests 720; these corroborate but do not prove the infinite-metric case.

value.rationale: The new main object is the entire natural algebra of real Dirac-diagonal coefficient operators on arbitrary Lipschitz-free spaces; the result gives a complete boundedness test and exact sharp operator norm from only three-point distances. It also identifies the norm of every coordinate selector, characterizes universal contractivity and sign unconditionality by metric geometry, and captures unbounded coordinate selectors on nondiscrete spaces. This is an all-parameter structural classification, not a chosen small numerical invariant or renaming of the star/L1 case.
